title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 24
paragraphs: This Arion, they say, who spent most of his time with Periander, conceived a desire to sail to Italy and Sicily, and after making a great deal of money there, he wished to return to Corinth. He set sail from Tarentum, and because he trusted Corinthians more than any other men, he hired a ship with a Corinthian crew. These men, out in the open sea, so the story goes, plotted to throw Arion overboard and seize his wealth. When he learned of it, he begged for his life, offering them his money in exchange. But he could not move them — the men conveying him told him either to kill himself on board, so that he might be buried on land, or to jump into the sea at once. Arion, driven to extremity, asked them, since they were of that mind, to let him stand on the deck in his full minstrel's costume and sing, promising to kill himself afterwards. Pleased at the thought of hearing the finest musician alive, they withdrew from the stern toward the middle of the ship. Arion put on his full minstrel's garb, took up his lyre, stood on the deck, and performed the Orthian strain; and when the song ended, he threw himself into the sea just as he was, in full costume. They went on sailing to Corinth — but a dolphin, they say, took him on its back and brought him safely to shore at Taenarum. Once on land he made his way to Corinth in his minstrel's dress, and there told the whole story. Periander, not believing him, kept Arion under guard and would not let him go anywhere, while he kept a close watch for the men who had carried him. When they arrived, he called them in and asked whether they had any news of Arion; and when they said he was safe in Italy and they had left him prospering at Tarentum, Arion suddenly appeared before them, just as he was when he jumped from the ship. Astonished, they could no longer deny anything when questioned. This is the tale told by the Corinthians and the Lesbians alike, and at Taenarum there is a small votive offering of Arion's — a bronze figure of a man on a dolphin's back.
